articles.summary: Galvanic facility utilizes automation to reduce production lead times of key components for civil, commercial and military aircraft engines KALISZ, Poland (Nov. 27, 2026) — Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, today announced the opening of a new galvanic facility at its Kalisz site, which manufactures precision components for multiple aircraft engine types serving civil, commercial and military operators around the world. By bringing galvanic processing capability in-house, Pratt & Whitney is strengthening control over its manufacturing process, improving quality, reducing production lead times and providing additional capacity to meet industry demand. Galvanic facilities perform a key function in aerospace manufacturing, enabling the metallic plating of components for durability and corrosion resistance. The new facility combines an automated galvanizing process with high standards of environmental and safety controls. It reduces the use of hazardous chemicals and manages water usage with a closed-loop system that enables full neutralization of water and removal of waste material. The facility also features advanced safety systems, including gas detection systems, redundant safety sensors and safety gates that automatically stop production lines. “The new galvanic facility marks another step in the development of Kalisz as a hub for advanced aerospace manufacturing and confirms Poland’s strategic importance to RTX,” said Wojciech Wasik, executive director, Board President, Pratt & Whitney Kalisz. “We are investing in technology, infrastructure and our employees’ skills, combining the highest standards of quality, safety and management of waste material.” Operating since 1992, the Kalisz site is an important part of Pratt & Whitney’s global manufacturing network, producing components for multiple engine types, ranging from turboprops to military engines. Kalisz is also a center of excellence for geared components, including the fan drive gear system featured on the Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engines that power the latest generation of single-aisle aircraft such as the Airbus A220, A320neo and Embraer E2 families. The project represents an investment of $12.5 million, which was supported by the Generator of Ecological Concepts, a joint program of Poland’s National Centre for Research and Development and the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management. Poland represents RTX's largest investment and employee base outside the United States, with more than 9,500 employees across its Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon businesses in-country. More than 1,700 employees are based in Kalisz. About Pratt & Whitney Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defence systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact corporatepr@rtx.com. SOURCE RTX

articles.summary: Contract supports design maturation and subsystem integration for emerging capabilityTUCSON, Ariz., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has been awarded an Other Transactional Authority (OTA) agreement by the U.S. Navy to advance the development of a next-generation, submarine-launched nuclear cruise missile, known as the Nuclear-Armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N).Under the contract, Raytheon's Advanced Technology team will transition work from early concept activities into a focused development phase that will mature the system's design, integrate key subsystems and prepare for future prototype demonstrations. The team will leverage its composable weapons approach, which uses mature, modular building blocks that can be integrated into new systems to reduce cycle time and accelerate missile development.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon selected to advance development of new submarine-launched missile for U.S. Navy

articles.summary: Multi-million-dollar investment will strengthen engineering and manufacturing capabilities for regional and transport aircraftBENGALURU, India, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, today broke ground at the Collins India Operations Center (CIOC) in Bengaluru for the country's first propeller maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) facility authorized by a foreign aerospace original equipment manufacturer. The facility will specialize in advanced propeller systems for ATR 42/72 regional aircraft and Airbus C295 military transport platforms throughout the Asia Pacific region.Collins' multi-million-dollar commitment to establish the MRO facility builds on more than $200 million the company has deployed in India over the last five years to offer a significant suite of enhanced aerospace services spanning engineering, manufacturing, testing and specialized aftermarket propeller maintenance.
articles.title: RTX's Collins Aerospace breaks ground on new propeller MRO facility in India

articles.summary: Reusable pod and affordable training round demonstrated for the U.S. ArmyTUCSON, Ariz., Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, demonstrated its DeepStrikeTM JR3 solution for the U.S. Army's Joint Reduced Range Rocket program during a third successful flight test. DeepStrike JR3 is designed to replace the U.S. Army's Reduced Range Practice Rocket. The latest test reinforces the system's reliability, affordability and readiness to meet the U.S. Army's growing training requirements.During the recent test at Yuma Proving Ground, Ariz., Raytheon rapidly fired multiple JR3 rounds and demonstrated several key performance attributes, including launch pod container reusability and maintainability, range, trajectory, accuracy and visibility of the marking solution to increase training effectiveness.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon advances Joint Reduced Range Rocket with third successful flight test

articles.summary: New technology to help operators detect and respond to threats fasterARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has been awarded a phase one contract from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to develop an all-optical processing system for the Photonic Integrated Circuit Architectures for Scalable System Objectives, or PICASSO, program.Under the contract, Raytheon's Advanced Technology team will design and demonstrate new photonic circuit technology that uses light rather than electricity to process signals. This means operators can detect threats sooner, respond more quickly and maintain better situational awareness in contested environments.
